why: Company release (2026-09-14): Q4 and FY2026 (FYE 2026-07-31) results Monday 2026-09-28, release about 4:30 PM ET, call 5:30 PM ET. Calendar row is correct.
session_evidence: Release 'at approximately 4:30 PM Eastern', call 5:30 PM Eastern on 2026-09-28: https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/09/14/3361077/33173/en/idt-corporation-to-report-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-results.html. Also on company site: https://www.idt.net/idt-corporation-to-report-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-year-2026-results/
where_to_look: The FY2027 Adjusted EBITDA guide is the September line, since this is the year-end print. Last September's print fell 18.4%. Look at segment trajectory: NRS POS terminal count and churn (37,200 terminals at FY25), BOSS Money transaction volume.
BOSS Money and net2phone app-store review volume and rankings as proxies for fintech remittance growth; remittance-tax (1% excise from 2026) effects on corridors.
Traditional Communications (BOSS Revolution calling, IDT Global) decline rate. It is the cash cow and a margin swing factor.
Share repurchase and dividend trail in the 10-Q and Form 4s; any NRS spin/strategic-alternatives chatter.
already_in_the_wire: FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA guide raised twice, to $150-152m (Q3 release 2026-06-03, https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/6/3/3306409/33173/en/idt-corporation-reports-third-quarter-fiscal-year-2026-results.html)
Record Q3 gross profit $122.5m; NRS op income +33%, Fintech +29%, net2phone +76%
trades_on: Mixed. The FY print (2025-09-29, -18.38%) slipped despite segment growth as EPS lapped a prior-year tax benefit (https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/idt-stock-slips-following-q4-earnings-despite-strong-segment-growth). Since then the guide has been raised at each print with reactions of -3.0%, -3.5% and +2.85%, so guide raises alone have not moved it up. Which line dominates is not established.
short_interest: 2.14% of float, days to cover 2.3, MarketBeat, settlement date not visible in the snippet (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/IDT/short-interest). Treat it as undated.
